mainTopic: Whether רבי יהודה is sure which thigh's גיד הנשה is forbidden, his sources for the right thigh, and aggadot about יעקב's wrestling
overview: רבי יהודה holds that גיד הנשה is forbidden in only one thigh. The גמרא asks whether he is sure it is the right thigh or unsure which one. רב אשי and רבינא push away a proof from the burning of sinews of a קרבן פסח: the burning could be for the fat, or for the outer nerve, which is only forbidden מדרבנן. A proof from a משנה about lashes uses the rule that רבי יהודה holds an התראת ספק does not count. That proof is turned aside, because another report of רבי יהודה, learned from the case of leftover פסח meat, says it does count. A ברייתא about two nerves from two thighs of two animals then proves that רבי יהודה is sure. His giving only forty lashes is explained by one nerve being smaller than a כזית. The גמרא gives several sources for the right thigh: the word 'הַיָּרֵךְ', and pictures of how the מלאך wrestled with יעקב. The רבנן say the מלאך came from behind and struck both thighs. The amud ends with aggadic teachings about the name גיד הנשה, יוסף's brothers, יעקב staying behind for small jars, and the rule that a תלמיד חכם should not go out alone at night. The source for that last rule continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב אשי: the burning is needed for the fat
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the משנה's rule of burning the sinews is really about the fat around the גיד הנשה, not the nerves of both legs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: That rule is needed only for the fat around the nerve. A ברייתא teaches that this fat is permitted, but the holy Jewish people treat it as forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes away the earlier proof that רבי יהודה is unsure. He says the burning in the משנה is for the fat, not for a doubtful second nerve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fat is permitted by Torah law, so it counts as real קרבן meat and may not simply be thrown away. But since Jews do not eat it, it is left over and must be burned. So the burning tells us nothing about whether רבי יהודה is unsure about the nerve.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for... (it is really about a different case)
Its fat, meaning the fat around the גיד הנשה
The Jewish people are holy, so they keep extra strictness
They treated it as forbidden as a custom

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
It is needed only for its fat,
phrases.notes: "It" is the משנה's rule that the sinews of a קרבן פסח get burned.

phrases.english: as it is taught: its fat is permitted,
but the Jewish people are holy and treated it as forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְשׇׁמְנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion: a new way to push away the proof from the burning of sinews.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the burning of sinews that רבי יהודה is unsure.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The burning can be explained by the fat, which is permitted by Torah law but not eaten by custom.

steps.title: רבינא: the burning is needed for the outer nerve
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the burning is about the outer nerve, which according to שמואל is forbidden only מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: That rule is needed only because of what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: there are two nerves. The inner one, next to the bone, is forbidden and one is punished for eating it. The outer one, next to the flesh, is forbidden but one is not punished for eating it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a different way to push away the same proof. The burning is for the outer nerve, not for the nerve of the other leg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The outer nerve is forbidden only by the רבנן, so by Torah law it is permitted קרבן meat. Since people do not eat it, it is left over and must be burned. Again, the burning does not show that רבי יהודה is unsure.

keyTerms.meaning: Two nerves (sinews)
The inner nerve, next to the bone (Torah prohibition)
The outer nerve, next to the flesh (rabbinic prohibition)
One is liable for it, meaning punished with lashes

steps.confusionAlert: Both nerves are called אסור. The difference is only whether one gets lashes: the inner one is a Torah prohibition, and the outer one is only rabbinic.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
It is needed only
for that which Rav Yehuda said Shmuel said,
as Rav Yehuda said Shmuel said:
There are two nerves:
the inner one, next to the bone, is forbidden,
and one is liable for it;
the outer one, next to the flesh, is forbidden,
but one is not liable for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְכִדְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different way to push away the same proof that רב אשי answered.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the burning of sinews that רבי יהודה is unsure.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The burning can be explained by the outer nerve, which is permitted by Torah law and forbidden only by the רבנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: שמואל's teaching of two nerves, one Torah-level and one rabbinic, is an important rule for the laws of גיד הנשה in general.

steps.title: A new source: lashes for eating from both nerves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: one who eats an olive-bulk from each leg's nerve gets eighty lashes, but רבי יהודה says only forty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If someone ate an olive-bulk from this nerve and an olive-bulk from that nerve, he gets eighty lashes. רבי יהודה says: He gets only forty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new משנה to try to answer whether רבי יהודה is sure or unsure. This step only quotes the source; the reasoning comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים hold both legs' nerves are forbidden, so eating from both gives two sets of forty lashes. רבי יהודה holds only one leg is forbidden, so he gives just forty. The question is how he can give even forty if he does not know which leg it is.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-bulk, the minimum amount for punishment
Receives (lashes)
Forty, the standard Torah punishment of lashes

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he ate an olive-bulk from this one
phrases.notes: "This one" and "that one" are the גיד הנשה of the right leg and of the left leg.

phrases.english: and an olive-bulk from that one,
he receives eighty lashes.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
He receives only forty.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אָכַל מִזֶּה כְּזַיִת וּמִזֶּה כְּזַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from burning was pushed away, the גמרא starts a fresh attempt using a different משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The question of whether רבי יהודה is sure or unsure which leg's nerve is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about lashes for eating an olive-bulk from each leg's nerve.

steps.title: Unsure would mean an uncertain warning
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יהודה were unsure, the warning before lashes would be uncertain, and he holds such a warning does not count. So he must be sure.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say he is sure. But if you say he is unsure, then the warning given to the sinner is an uncertain warning, and we know רבי יהודה holds that an uncertain warning is not a real warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the משנה proves that רבי יהודה is sure which leg is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lashes require a warning (התראה) right before the sin. If רבי יהודה did not know which leg was forbidden, each warning would be only a 'maybe', an התראת ספק. Since he holds that such a warning does not count, he could not give any lashes, yet he gives forty. So he must be sure which leg it is.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it makes sense if...
It is clear and obvious to him
He is in doubt about it
An uncertain warning, where it is not known for sure that the act is forbidden
The warning that must be given before a sin in order to give lashes

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה an התראת ספק does not count. So the fact that he gives forty lashes shows he is sure which leg's nerve is forbidden.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
it is obvious to him, that is fine.
But if you say
he is uncertain,
then it is an uncertain warning,
and we have heard that Rabbi Yehuda said:
an uncertain warning is not called a warning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא מִיפְשָׁט פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ – שַׁפִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the משנה quoted in the previous step proves the point.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה is sure which leg's nerve is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה gives forty lashes, combined with his view that an התראת ספק is not a valid warning.

steps.title: Source: striking or cursing two possible fathers
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה exempts someone who struck or cursed two possible fathers one after the other. This means he holds an uncertain warning does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: if he struck this one and then struck that one, or cursed this one and then cursed that one, or struck both at once, or cursed both at once, he is liable. רבי יהודה says: at once, he is liable; one after the other, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the claim from step 4 that רבי יהודה holds a התראת ספק is not a real warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a person who does not know which of two men is his father. When he hits both at once, he surely hit his father, so the warning is certain. When he hits them one after the other, each warning is a doubt, since this one may not be the father, and רבי יהודה exempts him. That shows he holds an uncertain warning does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: struck (hitting a parent is a capital crime)
cursed (cursing a parent is a capital crime)
at the same moment
one after the other
exempt from punishment

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is not saying the act is permitted. He is only saying the court cannot punish, because each warning was uncertain.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: if he struck this one,
phrases.notes: The case is a person who does not know which of two men is his father, so 'this one' could be his father or not.

phrases.english: and then struck that one,
or cursed this one,
and then cursed that one,
or struck both of them at once,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁקִּלֵּל שְׁנֵיהֶם בְּבַת אַחַת – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: or cursed both of them at once, he is liable.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בְּבַת אַחַת – חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: רבי יהודה says: at once, he is liable;
one after the other, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: הִכָּה אֶת זֶה, וְחָזַר וְהִכָּה אֶת זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for step 4's claim about רבי יהודה's view of התראת ספק.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה holds a התראת ספק is not a valid warning.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about striking or cursing two possible fathers one after the other.

steps.title: Our משנה follows a different report of רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תנא of the משנה about the nerves follows another תנא, who reports that רבי יהודה holds an uncertain warning does count.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תנא holds like the other תנא's version of רבי יהודה, who said that an uncertain warning is called a warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It says there are two reports of what רבי יהודה holds, and our משנה follows the other one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהודה holds a התראת ספק counts, then he could be unsure which leg's nerve is forbidden and still give lashes. So the proof from step 4 that he must be certain falls away. The גמרא will now show where this other report comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: the other תנא (a different teacher's report)
an uncertain warning, where it is not clear at warning time that a sin will happen
is called a warning, meaning it counts

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a ruling of a תנא can reach us in two versions, and the גמרא may match a משנה to one version.

phrases.english: This תנא holds
phrases.notes: 'This תנא' is the one who taught the משנה about the nerves of both legs, from step 3.

phrases.english: like the other תנא's version of רבי יהודה,
who said: an uncertain warning is called a warning.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּאִידַּךְ תַּנָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns aside the proof built in step 4, which rested on the ברייתא in step 5, by citing a different report of רבי יהודה's view.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The conclusion from step 4 that רבי יהודה must be certain which nerve is forbidden.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes every report of רבי יהודה rejects התראת ספק, but another תנא reports that he accepts it.

steps.title: Proof from leftover קרבן פסח meat
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה exempts from lashes for leaving over the פסח only because a positive command follows the prohibition. That means an uncertain warning would not have stopped lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'Do not leave any of it until morning…' The verse gives a positive command after a prohibition, to teach that one does not get lashes for it. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the other version of רבי יהודה, where an uncertain warning does count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When someone is warned not to leave the meat over, nobody can know yet that he will leave it until morning, because he could still eat it. So any warning here is uncertain. Yet רבי יהודה gives a different reason for no lashes, the positive command to burn it. This implies that without that command he would give lashes even with an uncertain warning.

keyTerms.meaning: do not leave over (the פסח meat)
a positive command (here, to burn what is left)
a negative command, a prohibition
give lashes

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: ״לֹא תוֹתִירוּ מִמֶּנּוּ עַד בֹּקֶר וְגוֹ׳״ –
phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: 'Do not leave any of it until morning, etc.'
phrases.notes: שמות 12:10. The rest of the פסוק says to burn whatever is left over by morning.

phrases.english: The verse comes to give a positive command
after a prohibition,
to say that one does not get lashes for it,
these are the words of רבי יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: לֹא תוֹתִירוּ מִמֶּנּוּ עַד בֹּקֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for step 6's claim that one report of רבי יהודה accepts התראת ספק.
steps.raayaObject: That according to one report, רבי יהודה holds a התראת ספק counts.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on leftover פסח meat, where רבי יהודה's only reason for no lashes is the positive command that follows.

steps.title: רבי יעקב gives a different reason for no lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב says there are no lashes for leaving over the meat because it is a prohibition broken without any action, not because of the positive command.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב says: this is not the reason. Rather, it is because this is a prohibition that involves no action, and for any prohibition that involves no action, one does not get lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with רבי יעקב, who agrees there are no lashes but disagrees about why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving meat over happens by doing nothing, so it is a לאו שאין בו מעשה, and such a prohibition does not bring lashes. The contrast helps the proof: רבי יהודה needed a special reason, the positive command, which shows he saw no problem with the uncertain warning itself.

keyTerms.meaning: this is not the reason
a prohibition broken without doing any action

steps.whatToRemember: According to this report, רבי יהודה exempts the leftover-meat case only because of the positive command. So he holds a התראת ספק counts, and our משנה can follow that view.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: לֹא מִן הַשֵּׁם הוּא זֶה,
phrases.english: רבי יעקב says: this is not for that reason,
rather, it is because it is
a prohibition that involves no action,
and any prohibition that involves no action,
one does not get lashes for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: לֹא מִן הַשֵּׁם הוּא זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא from step 7 with a dissenting reason, which highlights what רבי יהודה's own reason implies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are no lashes for leaving over the meat because it is a לאו שאין בו מעשה, and no prohibition of that kind brings lashes.

steps.title: A ברייתא about two nerves from two animals
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: someone ate two sciatic nerves from two thighs of two animals. The תנא קמא gives eighty lashes. רבי יהודה gives only forty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If someone ate two sciatic nerves from two thighs of two animals, he gets eighty lashes. רבי יהודה says he gets only forty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to settle whether רבי יהודה is certain or unsure about which thigh is forbidden. This step only quotes the source. The next step draws the proof from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each גיד is a separate forbidden item, so the תנא קמא gives forty lashes for each, eighty in total. רבי יהודה gives only forty. The גמרא will now study the wording "two thighs of two animals" to learn what רבי יהודה holds.

keyTerms.meaning: The sciatic nerve, which the Torah forbids eating
Thighs (hind legs) of the animal
Receives (lashes)
Eighty / forty lashes, meaning two sets of lashes or one set

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If someone ate two sciatic nerves
from two thighs of two animals,
he receives eighty lashes;
רבי יהודה says:
He receives only forty.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אָכַל שְׁנֵי גִידִין מִשְּׁתֵּי יְרֵכוֹת מִשְּׁתֵּי בְהֵמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The proof from the משנה about lashes (step 4) was pushed off in steps 6–8, by showing another version of רבי יהודה that accepts התראת ספק. So the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי יהודה is certain that the right thigh's גיד is the forbidden one
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about two גידין from two thighs of two animals

steps.title: The wording shows רבי יהודה is certain
steps.stepSummary: Saying 'two animals' means both nerves came from right thighs, so both are surely forbidden. Since רבי יהודה still gives lashes, he must be certain which thigh is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it says 'two thighs of two animals,' it is clear that both are forbidden. The case was needed for רבי יהודה's view. Learn from this that he is sure about it. Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the wording closely. It concludes that רבי יהודה is certain the right thigh's גיד is the one forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one nerve came from a right thigh and one from a left, there would be no need to say 'two animals,' since one animal has both. So the case must be two right thighs, and both nerves are surely forbidden. רבי יהודה gives lashes here, and he would not if he were unsure. So he must be certain. The גמרא accepts this.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious / clear
For the prohibition, meaning truly forbidden
It was needed (to be taught)
Learn from this; when repeated, the גמרא agrees

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא proves that רבי יהודה is certain, not in doubt, that the forbidden גיד is the one in the right thigh.

phrases.english: From the fact that it says 'from two thighs of two animals,'
it is clear that both are forbidden,
and the case was needed for רבי יהודה's view.
Learn from this that it is clear to him,
Yes, learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָאָמַר מִשְׁתֵּי יְרֵכוֹת מִשְּׁתֵּי בְהֵמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof from the ברייתא quoted in step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה is certain that the right thigh's גיד is forbidden by Torah law.

steps.title: Then why only forty lashes?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יהודה is sure both nerves are forbidden, he should give eighty lashes, not forty.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if it is clear to him, why does he get forty and no more? Let him get eighty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the conclusion it just reached. If both nerves are surely forbidden, why does רבי יהודה give only one set of lashes?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two definitely forbidden nerves should mean two sets of lashes, like the תנא קמא says. רבי יהודה's 'only forty' seems to fit better with doubt than with certainty, so it needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
And no more
Let him be lashed

phrases.english: But if it is clear to him,
why does he receive forty and no more?
Let him be lashed eighty!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ, אַמַּאי סוֹפֵג אַרְבָּעִים וְתוּ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading of the ברייתא from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that both nerves are surely forbidden according to רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two certain prohibitions should bring two sets of lashes, but רבי יהודה gives only one.

steps.title: One nerve was smaller than a כזית
steps.stepSummary: The case is where a nerve is smaller than a כזית. רבי יהודה holds there are no lashes for less than a כזית, even for a whole nerve.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a case where it does not have a כזית. As it was taught: If he ate it and it has no כזית, he is liable. רבי יהודה says: only if it has a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that one of the nerves was smaller than a כזית. That is why רבי יהודה gives only forty lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says eating a whole nerve brings lashes even if it is less than a כזית, because it is a complete item. רבי יהודה says lashes require a כזית. So the forty lashes come from the size issue, not from doubt about which thigh is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what case are we dealing with? (introduces a narrowed case)
An olive's volume, the usual minimum amount for punishment
Liable (to punishment)

phrases.english: Here, what case are we dealing with?
Such as where it does not have a כזית,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: אֲכָלוֹ וְאֵין בּוֹ כְּזַיִת – חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: As it was taught: If he ate it and it has no כזית, he is liable,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ כְּזַיִת.
phrases.english: רבי יהודה says: Not until it has a כזית.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן – כְּגוֹן דְּלֵית בּוֹ כְּזַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Forty lashes looked like it came from doubt about which thigh.
steps.terutzMaskana: Forty lashes comes from one nerve being less than a כזית, which רבי יהודה does not punish.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה holds that only the right thigh's nerve is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know רבי יהודה is certain, the גמרא asks for his source. This sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being certain that the right thigh is forbidden requires a basis. The גמרא wants to know where in the Torah this comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the reason?

phrases.english: And what is the reason?
phrases.notes: The question is why רבי יהודה says it is specifically the right thigh.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטַעְמָא מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that רבי יהודה is certain, and asks for his source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for רבי יהודה's view that the right thigh is forbidden

steps.title: "הַיָּרֵךְ" means the most important thigh
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the פסוק says "הַיָּרֵךְ", 'the thigh,' which points to the most important thigh, the right one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The verse says "the thigh", meaning the most important thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. The word "הַיָּרֵךְ" in the פסוק points to the most important thigh, which is the right one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra letter ה, 'the,' shows that the פסוק means one special thigh, not just any thigh. The most important thigh is the right one. This is why רבי יהודה is certain and not in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: The most important one (literally 'the right-hand' or 'the chosen')

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה's view comes from the word "הַיָּרֵךְ": the Torah forbids the גיד of the most important thigh, the right one.

phrases.english: רבא said:
The verse says "the thigh"
the most important of the thighs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אָמַר קְרָא ״הַיָּרֵךְ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word "הַיָּרֵךְ" with ה shows the Torah means the most important thigh, the right one.

steps.title: How the רבנן read the word 'the thigh'
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use 'הירך' to point to the nerve that spreads through the whole thigh, the inner one. This leaves out the outer nerve.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? They say 'the thigh' means the nerve whose prohibition spreads through the whole thigh. That leaves out the outer nerve, which is not included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question. The רבנן say both thighs are forbidden, so what do they learn from the word 'הַיָּרֵךְ'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא used 'the thigh' to mean the right thigh, but the רבנן forbid both sides. So they read 'the' differently: it points to the inner nerve, which runs through the entire thigh. The outer nerve is not the one the פסוק is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis, the majority view that argues on רבי יהודה
Its prohibition spreads out
To exclude, to leave out
The outer nerve of the thigh

steps.confusionAlert: The רבנן are not arguing about which thigh here. They forbid both thighs. They only use 'the' to pick between the inner nerve and the outer nerve.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: He means: how do the Rabbis, who forbid both thighs, use the word 'the thigh'?

phrases.english: [It means] that one whose prohibition spreads through the whole thigh,
to exclude the outer [nerve], which does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the opposing view uses the same word רבא used for רבי יהודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What do the רבנן learn from 'הַיָּרֵךְ'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It points to the inner nerve that spreads through the whole thigh, which leaves out the outer nerve.

steps.title: Wrestling: the hand reaches the right thigh
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי learns it from 'בְּהֵאָבְקוֹ עִמּוֹ'. When you hug someone to wrestle, your hand reaches his right thigh.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: the פסוק says 'as he wrestled with him'. That is like a man who hugs his friend, and his hand reaches his friend's right thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second reason for רבי יהודה's view that only the right thigh is forbidden. This reason comes from the way the wrestling happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא learned 'right' from one word. רבי יהושע בן לוי learns it from the picture of the fight instead. When two people face each other and grab around, the attacker's hand lands on the other person's right side.

keyTerms.meaning: As he wrestled
Hugs, wraps his arms around
The right 'spoon' of the thigh, the hip socket area

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The verse says, 'as he wrestled with him' –
like a person who hugs his friend,

phrases.aramaic: וְיָדוֹ מַגַּעַת לְכַף יְמִינוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ.
phrases.english: and his hand reaches the right thigh-socket of his friend.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the question in step 13, different from רבא's.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does רבי יהודה say the right thigh?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The way people wrestle, by hugging, puts the hand on the other person's right thigh.

steps.title: The angel looked like a גוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני says the מלאך looked like a גוי. A Jew keeps a גוי traveling with him on his right side, so the מלאך was at יעקב's right.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: he looked to יעקב like a גוי. As the Master said: a Jew who is joined by a גוי on the road keeps him on his right.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third reason why it was the right thigh. יעקב kept the stranger on his right side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explanation is about where the מלאך was standing before the fight. יעקב thought he was a גוי, and the rule is to keep a גוי on your right. So the מלאך was on that side and struck the right thigh.

keyTerms.meaning: He appeared to him as, looked like
Attached himself to him, joined him
Keeps him at his right side

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said:
He appeared to him like a gentile,
phrases.notes: The 'he' is the מלאך who wrestled with יעקב.

phrases.english: as the Master said:
A Jew who is joined by a gentile on the road –
keeps him at his right.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר: כְּגוֹי נִדְמָה לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another different answer to the same question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does רבי יהודה say the right thigh?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מלאך looked like a גוי, and a Jew keeps a גוי on his right, so he struck the right thigh.

steps.title: The angel looked like a Torah scholar
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר אחא, speaking before רב פפא in the name of רבא בר עולא, says the מלאך looked like a תלמיד חכם. A student does not walk on his teacher's right, so the מלאך was at יעקב's right.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר אחא said before רב פפא in the name of רבא בר עולא: he looked to יעקב like a תלמיד חכם. As the Master said: one who walks at his teacher's right is an ignorant person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a fourth and final reason for the right thigh. This time יעקב gave the stranger the right side out of respect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same idea of position as the last step, but for the opposite reason. Before, the right side was for safety; here it is for honor. The respected person walks on the right, so the מלאך was at יעקב's right and touched his right thigh.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah scholar
His teacher
An ignorant, unmannered person

steps.whatToRemember: There are four explanations for why רבי יהודה forbids only the right thigh: רבא from the word 'הַיָּרֵךְ', and three from the story itself (wrestling, a גוי on the right, a תלמיד חכם on the right).
steps.confusionAlert: 'Walking at his teacher's right is a בּוּר' means the student should not take the right side. The teacher gets the right side, so יעקב put the stranger on his right.

phrases.aramaic: רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַחָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Aḥa, before Rav Pappa,
said in the name of Rava bar Ulla:
He appeared to him like a Torah scholar,
as the Master said:
One who walks at the right of his teacher –
this is an ignoramus.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַחָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא בַּר עוּלָּא אָמַר: כְּתַלְמִיד חָכָם נִדְמָה לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 17, but explains the right-side position through honor instead of safety.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does רבי יהודה say the right thigh?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מלאך looked like a תלמיד חכם, whom יעקב kept on his right out of respect, so he struck the right thigh.

steps.title: The רבנן: the angel came from behind and struck both thighs
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן picture the מלאך attacking יעקב from behind, so he struck both thighs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say: the מלאך came from behind יעקב and struck him on both thighs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the רבנן picture the fight. This fits their view that the nerve is forbidden in both thighs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי and the others explained why only the right thigh was hurt. The רבנן forbid the nerve in both thighs, so they need a picture where both were hurt. If the מלאך grabbed יעקב from behind, his hands could reach both thighs.

keyTerms.meaning: From behind him
He struck him and pushed the nerve out of place (connected to the word נָשֶׁה)
On both of them, meaning both thighs

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: he came from behind him,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the מלאך who wrestled with יעקב.

phrases.english: and struck him on both of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, מֵאֲחוֹרֵיהּ אֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list of how each opinion pictures the fight. After the right-thigh explanations, this gives the רבנן's both-thighs picture.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מלאך attacked from behind and hit both thighs, which fits the רבנן's view that both nerves are forbidden.

steps.title: What do the רבנן learn from 'as he wrestled with him'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the רבנן do with the words 'בְּהֵאָבְקוֹ עִמּוֹ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they learn from these words, 'as he wrestled with him'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to set up the next step. The רבנן do not use 'בְּהֵאָבְקוֹ עִמּוֹ' to prove the right thigh, so what do these words teach them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16, רבי יהושע בן לוי used these words to show the right thigh was hurt. The רבנן reject that, but the words are still in the פסוק. The גמרא assumes every word of the תורה teaches something, so it asks what the רבנן learn from them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As he wrestled with him,' words in the פסוק about יעקב's fight
What do they learn from it?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, this phrase "as he wrestled with him"
what do they learn from it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, הַאי ״בְּהֵאָבְקוֹ עִמּוֹ״ מַאי דָּרְשִׁי בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since the רבנן explained the fight without these words, the גמרא asks what these words teach them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the רבנן learn from 'בְּהֵאָבְקוֹ עִמּוֹ', since they do not use it for the right thigh.

steps.title: The dust of the fight rose to the Throne of Glory
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use the words for a different teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי: the dust of the wrestling rose up to the כסא הכבוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it for another teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי. He said: this teaches that the dust from their feet rose all the way up to the כסא הכבוד. Here it says 'בְּהֵאָבְקוֹ עִמּוֹ', and there (נחום) it says 'and clouds are the dust of His feet.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן use 'בְּהֵאָבְקוֹ' for a different lesson. The word sounds like 'אָבָק', dust, and it teaches that the dust of the fight rose up to the כסא הכבוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בְּהֵאָבְקוֹ' contains the letters of 'אָבָק', dust. A פסוק in נחום uses 'אֲבַק' for the clouds near הקב"ה. Linking the two words teaches that the dust of the fight reached up to הקב"ה's throne. So the words are not wasted for the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
For that other teaching
Dust
The Throne of Glory, הקב"ה's throne
It is written here... and it is written there: linking two פסוקים that share a word

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same רבי יהושע בן לוי from step 16, but a different teaching of his. The רבנן accept this teaching even though they reject his right-thigh lesson.

phrases.english: They need it for the other teaching
of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
This teaches that they raised the dust from their feet
phrases.notes: 'They' means יעקב and the מלאך, kicking up dust as they wrestled.

phrases.english: all the way up to the Throne of Glory.
It is written here: "As he wrestled with him,"
and it is written there: "And the clouds are the dust of His feet."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לִכְאִידַּךְ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20 by giving the רבנן a different use for the words.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן use 'בְּהֵאָבְקוֹ' to teach that the dust of the fight rose to the כסא הכבוד, by linking it to 'אֲבַק רַגְלָיו' in נחום.
steps.whatToRemember: Each opinion has its own picture of the fight. The רבנן say the מלאך came from behind and hit both thighs, and they use 'בְּהֵאָבְקוֹ' to teach that the dust rose to the כסא הכבוד.

steps.title: Why it is called גיד הנשה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי explains that the nerve is called גיד הנשה because it slipped out of its place and moved up.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Why is it called גיד הנשה? Because it slipped (נָשָׁה) from its place and went up. And so the פסוק says: 'Their strength has slipped away (נָשְׁתָה), they became like women.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי, about the name גיד הנשה. He says 'נָשֶׁה' means 'moved away,' because the nerve slipped out of its place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic: the meaning of the name, not which thigh. He proves that 'נָשָׁה' means 'left' or 'slipped away' from a פסוק in ירמיהו. There, the strength of the soldiers 'נָשְׁתָה,' it left them.

keyTerms.meaning: The sciatic nerve, which may not be eaten
Slipped away, moved out of its place
And so the פסוק says: brings a פסוק to show how a word is used

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Why is its name called gid hanashe?
Because it slipped from its place and went up,
and so the verse says:
"Their strength has slipped away, they have become like women."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 51:30, about the soldiers of בבל losing their strength.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: לָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since a teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי was just quoted, the גמרא brings another teaching of his about גיד הנשה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The name גיד הנשה comes from 'נָשָׁה', slipped away, because the nerve moved out of its place.

steps.title: The איסור of גיד הנשה spread to all of ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא reads a פסוק in ישעיהו as a hint to גיד הנשה and to its איסור spreading to all Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: What does the פסוק mean, 'He sent a word to יעקב, and it fell upon ישראל'? 'He sent a word to יעקב' means גיד הנשה. 'And it fell upon ישראל' means its איסור spread to all of ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: Another teaching about גיד הנשה. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains a פסוק as a hint to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'word sent to יעקב' is what happened to יעקב himself: his nerve was hurt. 'Fell upon ישראל' means the result reached all his descendants. The איסור to eat it applies to every Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written? Opens an explanation of a פסוק
A word, a matter
Its איסור spread out

steps.whatToRemember: The name גיד הנשה means the nerve 'slipped' out of place. What happened to יעקב became an איסור for all of כלל ישראל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״דָּבָר שָׁלַח בְּיַעֲקֹב וְנָפַל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל״?
phrases.english: What is the meaning of what is written: "He sent a word to Jacob, and it fell upon Israel"?
"He sent a word to Jacob": this is the gid hanashe,
"And it fell upon Israel": its prohibition spread to all of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with more teachings about גיד הנשה, now from a פסוק in נביאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'דָּבָר שָׁלַח בְּיַעֲקֹב' hints at גיד הנשה, and 'וְנָפַל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל' teaches that its איסור applies to all of ישראל.

steps.title: יוסף's steward slaughters and removes the גיד הנשה in front of the brothers
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains יוסף's words 'וּטְבוֹחַ טֶבַח וְהָכֵן' as orders to show the brothers that the slaughter was done properly and that the גיד הנשה was removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: What is meant by the פסוק 'and slaughter the animals, and prepare'? It means: show them the place of the slaughter. 'And prepare' means: take out the גיד הנשה in front of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא gives a second teaching. He reads two words in יוסף's command to his steward as two separate instructions about kosher meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וּטְבוֹחַ טֶבַח' means: let them see the cut of the שחיטה so they know it was done right. 'וְהָכֵן' means: remove the גיד הנשה while they watch. יוסף wanted his brothers to feel sure they could eat the meat.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Slaughter the animals and prepare.' This is יוסף's order to his steward.
Uncover, expose to view.
The place on the neck where the animal was slaughtered.
Take out, remove.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina said:
What is that which is written: 'And slaughter the animals, and prepare'?
Expose to them the place of the slaughter,
'And prepare' means: remove the sciatic nerve in front of them,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from the same רבי who gave the hint to גיד הנשה in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יוסף told his steward to show the brothers the שחיטה and to remove the גיד הנשה in front of them.

steps.title: This fits the view that גיד הנשה was forbidden to בני נח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's reading only works for the opinion that the איסור of גיד הנשה already applied before מתן תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows the one who said that גיד הנשה was forbidden to בני נח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short comment showing which side of an earlier argument this teaching fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brothers lived before מתן תורה, when they were still counted as בני נח. If they cared about the גיד הנשה, then the איסור must have applied to them already. This matches the view that it was forbidden to בני נח, and it does not fit the view that it was first forbidden at סיני.

keyTerms.meaning: This follows the one who said...
Descendants of נח. Here it means people living before מתן תורה.
Was forbidden.

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean that non-Jews today are forbidden to eat גיד הנשה. It is about whether יעקב's family already kept this איסור before the תורה was given.

phrases.aramaic: כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה נֶאֱסָר לִבְנֵי נֹחַ.
phrases.english: According to the one who said the sciatic nerve was forbidden to the descendants of Noah.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה נֶאֱסָר לִבְנֵי נֹחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places step 24's reading on one side of the argument about when גיד הנשה became forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's reading matches the view that גיד הנשה was forbidden to בני נח.

steps.title: יעקב stayed behind for small jars
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that יעקב was left alone because he went back for small jars. This teaches that צדיקים value their money more than their own bodies.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And יעקב was left alone.' רבי אלעזר said: He stayed behind for small jars. From here we learn that צדיקים hold their money dearer than their bodies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the wrestling story. רבי אלעזר explains why יעקב ended up alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר reads 'וַיִּוָּתֵר' as 'he stayed behind': יעקב had already crossed the river and went back for small, cheap jars. He even risked danger for them. From this we learn how much צדיקים value their possessions.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he was left' or 'he remained.'
Small jars or pitchers.
From here we learn.
Their money or possessions.

phrases.english: 'And Jacob was left alone,'
Rabbi Elazar said:
That he remained behind for small jars,
From here we learn about the righteous
that their money is dearer to them than their bodies,

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיִּוָּתֵר יַעֲקֹב לְבַדּוֹ אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the wrestling story after the short side teachings about יוסף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יעקב stayed behind for small jars, which shows that צדיקים value their money more than their bodies.

steps.title: Why do צדיקים care so much about their money?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why צדיקים care so much about even small belongings.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why all this?
steps.whatsHappening: A short question that sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It sounds odd for a צדיק to care so much about money. The question stops us from thinking the lesson is about greed.

keyTerms.meaning: And why so much?

phrases.english: And why all this?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל כָּךְ לָמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 26's lesson.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why צדיקים value their money so highly.

steps.title: Because they never take what is not theirs
steps.stepSummary: צדיקים value their possessions because every bit was earned honestly. They never reach for stolen property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they do not stretch out their hands to stolen property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: their money is precious because it is completely honest money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who never steals has only what he worked for, so every small thing matters to him. The point is honesty, not greed.

keyTerms.meaning: Stretch out their hands, meaning reach out to take.
Stolen property, robbery.

steps.whatToRemember: יעקב went back for small jars because a צדיק's money is all honestly earned, so even small things are precious to him.

phrases.english: Because they do not stretch out their hands to stolen property.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין פּוֹשְׁטִין יְדֵיהֶן בְּגָזֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They never take what is not theirs, so what they have is precious to them.

steps.title: A תלמיד חכם should not go out alone at night
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק learns from יעקב's night wrestling that a תלמיד חכם should not go out alone at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And a man wrestled with him until the break of dawn.' רבי יצחק said: From here we learn that a תלמיד חכם should not go out alone at night.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק draws a practical lesson from the wrestling story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יעקב was alone, it was night, and he was attacked and hurt. From this we learn that a תלמיד חכם should not walk out alone at night.

keyTerms.meaning: And he wrestled.
Daybreak, dawn.
A Torah scholar.
Alone, by himself.

phrases.english: 'And a man wrestled with him until the break of dawn,'
Rabbi Yitzḥak said:
From here we learn regarding a Torah scholar
that he should not go out alone at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיֵּאָבֵק אִישׁ עִמּוֹ עַד עֲלוֹת הַשָּׁחַר אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next words of the same פסוק and draws a new lesson.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical guideline of caution for תלמידי חכמים, and the next step will look for another source for it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם should not go out alone at night.

steps.title: רבי אבא בר כהנא gives a different source
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר כהנא says the same lesson comes from a different פסוק. The פסוק itself comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר כהנא said: From here.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. רבי אבא בר כהנא is about to give his own source for the rule, and the פסוק follows right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees with the rule but learns it from a different place. This tells us he thinks some other פסוק teaches the lesson better than יעקב's wrestling.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, meaning from this source.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא אָמַר מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: From here:

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the rule in step 29.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a תלמיד חכם should not go out alone at night.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A different פסוק, quoted on the next amud.
